SABRENT 4TB Rocket NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive (SB-ROCKET-4TB) I tested this in a USB 3 adapter on my MacBook Air. Why would I do that? What could possibly be the point?

Well, I couldn't persuade my son to pull his m.2 drive and test this one against it (haven't yet, anyway - next time he wants a favor bad enough to stop playing Dark Souls to as me for it, I will update with results).

Couldn't afford a thunderbolt adapter (what is up with that). So my question became whether USB 3 is fast enough for an m.2 drive to make a difference versus a SATA SSD.

And it is. The Nvme drive clocks in at 400-500 mbps over the SATA drive's 240 top speed. And the price of the drives plus their adapters is about equal per gigabyte.
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT 4TB Rocket NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive (SB-ROCKET-4TB)

text_fidelity_a: SamData 32GB USB Flash Drives 4 Pack 32GB Thumb Drives Memory Stick Jump Drive with LED Light for Storage and Backup (4 Colors: Black Blue Green Purple) This unit does work, but it is too slow for me to recommend it to others. When writing music onto it from my Windows computer, the write speed was slow enough to repeatedly drop the data transfer rate all the way to zero. Other manufacturers' flash drives do not do that; they keep on going. The read speed is slow enough that it causes my car's infotainment system (2019 model year) to sometimes hang up. Indeed, at one point, it caused my backup camera to go to all black for a minute or two. Note that some other reviewers are apparently unware of what flash memory is like. It has a limited number of times that it can be written (rewritten), and it will wear out if you try to use it as a substitute for a SSD. It also isn't going to be nearly as fast as a SSD. Flash memory is most appropriate for putting mp3 files into your car's infotainment system and other applications that are write only a few times but read many times.
text_fidelity_b: SamData 32GB USB Flash Drives 4 Pack 32GB Thumb Drives Memory Stick Jump Drive with LED Light for Storage and Backup (4 Colors: Black Blue Green Purple)

Amazon Basics Standby UPS 600VA 360W Surge Protector Battery Power Backup - 8 Outlets, Black I'm pleased with the performance and features of this UPS. While it does not have the features that my other UPS's have (such as a screen that displays battery status, load, etc.) that's a plus, since I don't often use, or need, the info on the screen. This has just a simple on/off button, a mute button, and basic LED indicators that show if it's on line power or battery power.

It comes with the battery leads detached. Before use you need to remove the battery access panel (very simple -- just two screws) and connect the battery (also a very simple process).

I use it to for my router and cable modem so I can maintain Internet access and wifi during a power outage. I've simulated a power outage and both the modem and router didn't skip a beat. While this has a smaller capacity than the UPS's I use for my PCs, the 1000VA 550W specs are more than adequate to maintain a long run time given the light load.

One quibble -- and I have the same one with most UPS systems -- is that the outlets are too closely spaced, making it difficult to use all of them when plugging in devices that have a wall wart at the end. I would also have liked to see the outlets be color coded so you can more easily tell the difference between the bank of outlets that are surge protected only, and the bank that is surge/battery protected.

Those quibbles aside, it's been a good performer that provides all the features needed at a decent price.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Standby UPS 600VA 360W Surge Protector Battery Power Backup - 8 Outlets, Black

Belkin N300 Wireless N Router (Latest Generation) (F9K1002) Bought this for my mother who has a small 2 bedroom apartment. Has been installed for over 3 weeks now. It was so very easy to install, simple instructions, did not have to adjust any settings. We just attached it to the DSL modem, loaded the CD into each computer that was going to use the network, followed the simple instructions, works great. We did have a problem trying to set up an account, which we still have not been able to do. May call later for assistance if we find it would be helpful to have an account, but so far everything works great.

We have had my mother's desktop computer (also running wireless now), her notebook computer, my notebook computer and the printer all running on the network at the same time. There was absolutely no degradation in service, have never had a problem with disconnects even with all computers running at the same time and two of the computers sending documents to the printer. This includes using one of the notebook computers at the furthest location in the apartment away from the router as possible. The only problem we have is the slower Verizon DSL service compared to the faster Verizon FIOS service I have at my house, so not a Belkin problem. Too bad my mother can't get FIOS. But her internet access is as fast as it was when it was attached directly to the modem.

Would highly recommend this product.

5/28/2015 - Just found this review I wrote in 2011. My mother is still using the same Belkin N150, still works great even if we have 3 computers running at the same time. The retirement community she lives in switched voice/Internet carriers about 6 months ago. Saw no difference in performance. Highly recommend.

Logitech HD Laptop Webcam C615 with Fold-and-Go Design, 360-Degree Swivel, 1080p Camera I was able to compare this directly to the Logitech C525. They both have the same "fold and go" design, but I was surprised that the C615 is a bit heavier, and I think a millimeter or two thicker. It's well worth it, because the optics are better, and not just better because the resolution is higher - the quality is simply better.

The tripod mount is a nice addition over the C525, adding versitility in positioning. I suppose this would also help you set it up as a hidden camera, or just keep a pile of dirty laundry out of the view mounting on your laptop might otherwise provide.

As others have mentioned, there is a USB extender, which is nice. However, I would much rather have seen a long (or even a very short) cable provided with a microUSB connection to the actual device, allowing the device to become truly portable, rather than having a nice foldable, portable device with a cumbersome cord permanently attached. The user could then use the same cable they charge their smartphone with. Thankfully, the cord is placed in such a way that allows for full 360 degree rotation.

Note that although you can record 1080 videos with this device, you can only chat in 720 - another consideration if you just want this for Skype or another chat program.

Overall, this is the most appealing webcam on the market to me. The most important thing is that it can be tossed in a bag or pocket with other electronics without having to worry about the lens getting scratched.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech HD Laptop Webcam C615 with Fold-and-Go Design, 360-Degree Swivel, 1080p Camera

text_fidelity_a:
CablesOnline 6ft 2-RCA Male to 2-RCA Female Red/White Audio Extension Cable, (AV-E406RW) These are pretty much as basic an RCA cable you can find that will extend the length of your existing RCA cables without the need for another male-to-male adapter. While for components that have RCA hookups that allow you to use any RCA cable that your can find, I would recommend buying a single longer cable as every connection point is a place for potential signal loss. However, for components that have their RCA cables integrated with the device, you have little choice but to buy an extender such as this. Turntables, especially the older variety, are the most notable components that have this configuration, and since most people like to be able to play records from a location that is easy to reach and has plenty of headroom, this is often far away from your receiver and the built-in cables on the turntable are usually far too short for this. This is why these cables are a perfect way to add an extra 3' while only introducing one additional connection in your linkage, where using a standard RCA cable with a male-to-male adapter introduces two.

Also, since the cables which are connected to turntables are almost always of bare-bones quality with the minimum gauge of copper necessary to carry a signal (that's assuming the wire is made from copper at all, and not from some other cheaper alloy), these are probably going to be the same gauge. Your connection is only as good as the weakest link, so buying some thick gauge cable that is made out of magnetically polarized copper probably would only serve to drive the price up with no actual benefit to you except for being able to brag about them. Therefore, this RCA cable extenders is all that you really need and will spare you the embarrassment of spending money on something that you actually do not need at all. Some "high end" users might complain about them being of a small gauge because they have convinced themselves that they have to use overpriced Monster cables to connect their gear to be able to fully enjoy it., but I don't necessarily buy into this. True, good cable makes a difference, especially when you are sending a signal over a longer distance (10' or more) chances are the mid-grade cable of 16 gauge copper wire with gold plated contacts is all you're going to need. This cable solves your short cable problem while telling the world "I am care about how my music sounds, but I am neither a sucker nor a fool!"
text_fidelity_b: CablesOnline 6ft 2-RCA Male to 2-RCA Female Red/White Audio Extension Cable, (AV-E406RW)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony Ultimate All in One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer Okay. At first I was not impressed with the Harmony Ultimate. After getting the system up and going, however, I love it.

Desired goal: control two entertainment systems in two rooms with four remotes -- two in each room.

3/29/16 update: I thought having a single remote talking to a single hub was a drawback. But the app on my iPhone is so effective, it's really a second remote for no extra cost. I don't even touch the actual remote that came with the system. That's for the wife, who has taken to the system easily and understands how to work it. I now love my system. Five stars.

3/17/16 Logitech Ultimate Remote w/Hub
Cons:
1. Only one remote can be paired with each hub. Want the wife to have her own remote on one side of the room and you to have another, both controlling the same equipment? Forget it. You can't.
2. Two hubs cannot talk to each other. So you buy two remotes and two hubs, thinking they will talk to each other over WiFi? Forget it. They can't.
3. Pricey at list. Acceptable when on sale ($120 off is nice)

Pros:
1. Excellent phone app. You do all programming from the phone after you create a Logitech cloud account. This gives you control of your system if your phone can reach the internet.
2. Excellent desktop app. Logitech has given up trying to use browsers; you use genuine local apps on your phone and laptop.
3. Easy to set up: Enter MFG and Model number for each device. Done. Full remote buttons download for each device.
4. Touch screen on both the remote and the app has "gestures" with one- or two-finger swiping to control devices. This is nice and unexpected.
5. Colorful
6. Recharges in the cradle -- no more AAA batteries!
7. Wakes up when you pick it up
8. Backlit buttons
9. Haptic feedback when a virtual button is pressed
10. Phone app is great for setup and works as a second remote.

Setting up the first remote was wonderful and very exciting. I couldn't wait to expand the system with my second hub and its remote to create a really capable, flexible system. When the second hub failed to talk to the first hub and I discovered that I had purchased two systems that cannot talk to each other, my elation went to mild disappointment.

Sequence to set up:

1. Create an account with Logitech Harmony at myharmony.com
2. Download the Harmony phone app and download the desktop exe to your laptop.
3. Log in to the account
4. Name and connect the first hub with you WiFi router password
5. Add devices to the room's hub by entering the Manufacturer and the Model number for each device
a. These devices can be far more than AV devices, including lights, blinds, thermostats and other things to a limit of 15.
b. Each device can be renamed for accurate familiarity
6. Create "Activities" for the devices you want to control:
I.e., "Blu-ray Living Rm"
a. it will ask first, "what devices are involved in this activity?"
b. checkbox "AV receiver Living Rm," "TV Living Rm," and "Blu-ray Living Rm"
c. the app asks, "Which input for the TV?" and "Which input for the AV Receiver?" and "Which device controls the volume?"
d. click "run test" to see if everything shuts off and turns back on correctly
e. if it's good, click "yes." Good to go to create next activity.

After you get one room's devices entered and working, if you have a second hub and remote, program it separately in the next room. You can rename the hubs using the desktop exe, but not from the phone app. This is very helpful if you are using the phone as a second remote. You'll have to switch hubs on the phone if you go from one room to another.

You can reorder the activities on both the phone and the remote for most logical order for that room
You can edit buttons and gestures and more.
You can add delay time if a unit needs more time to warm up before it can receive a command
You can change the timeout for the remote to go into standby
You can use your phone as a fully functional remote, but you do have to select which hub you want to talk to.
The Hub connects wirelessly to your WiFi router. It also acts as a giant IR blaster to send commands to the devices. It also has two 2.5mm mono sub-mini plug sockets and two "mini blaster" IR emitters that plug into these sockets so you can send IR to other places.

If you have a device in another room that needs to be controlled, you can extend one of the mini-blasters using an inexpensive 2.5mm extension cord like the 5-meter [[ASIN:B003OSR5TE kenable 2.5mm Stereo Jack Plug to 2.5mm Jack Socket Extension Cable 5m (~16.5 feet)]] or a wireless remote IR extension system like the [[ASIN:B0087S9CJ2 Monoprice 109194 Wireless Dual Band IR Remote Control Extender Upto 328-Feet]].

This wired or wireless extension to another room would be moot if the hubs talked to each other.

What Logitech needs to make happen is to allow multiple remotes to talk to multiple hubs and for the hubs to talk to each other. They've been promising this added capability since at least 2013 on their forums, but so far, it's one remote to one hub and workarounds.

Logitech should not market this as "Ultimate." It's very capable, but also not quite as flexible as required.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony Ultimate All in One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer

Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest. I'm a huge fan of Microsoft keyboards. Never been much of a fan of their office productivity software, but when it comes to keyboards, Microsoft fits my needs to a T. I'm using the Microsoft Digital Media Pro keyboard which (I believe) was discontinued years ago. A shame, since it has so many useful features.

But out with the old and in with the new. I tried and did not care for the previous generation of ergonomic split keyboards from Microsoft. At first glance the Sculpt looked to be a better design. The divide between the two sets of keys did not appear to be as pronounced, and my hands seemed to fit the keyboard very well. Love the feel of the pad on the wrist rest area!

Installation was straightforward, although getting the items out of the box was a challenge. I was happy to see that the necessary batteries were included - nothing worse than having to go hunt for batteries before you can start to use a new device.

The keyboard feel strongly reminded me of a laptop. For some, that may be a good feature. For me it is not. The flat keys and shorter throw makes typing feel "unnatural." I know that sounds vague, but it's the best way I can describe it.

This odd feel translated itself into a much slower typing speed - cut my throughput by about half. Since I write reports for a living, that's a rather big issue.

I also could not come to grips with the function key placement, size and meager supply of ancillary keys. That's a feature I love with my current Media Pro keyboard in that I can map pretty much any of the ample number of multimedia keys to any function I choose, or even a URL. For example, to start SPSS, Excel and WP I press one key. Another single keypress also opens my browser and my Amazon cart URL (and yes, the lettering on that particular key is pretty much worn completely off from use).

Still, if I was forced to, I could live with the keyboard. I could not, under any circumstances, live with the mouse in this set. Feels poor, lacks refinement, and far less versatile than my Logitech M500. I tried my best to get used to the Sculpt mouse, but just grew to hate it the longer I used it.

Now, my opinions are certainly affected by my current choices in keyboards and mice since I've been using them for years and years. I've changed PCs at least three times, but have retained the same keyboard and mouse since they have worked so well. If you have less keyboard/mouse "muscle memory" perhaps the Sculpt will fit the bill. The build quality seems decent, and if they are as reliable as other Microsoft keyboards, it will continue to work for some time. But for me, I just can't move the approval meter past "meh" for the keyboard and "dud" for the mouse. Three stars.

The design allows me to leave the slim ends plugged into my laptop all the time, and then I can put the longer ends on whatever I want to plug in. The result? Much less stress on the ports, since I’m not constantly plugging things and and taking them out.

I’m using the adapters with my MacBook Pro (13-inch, 2017, Four Thunderbolt 3 Ports). I use one adapter for the power cable and one adapter for a hub. The hub has an external monitor (HDMI) and a few USB-A peripherals plugged into it.

The adapters can be used side by side. I have another style of adapter that is too bulky to allow use of the port next to it, so I appreciate the slimmer design of the ZRSE adapters.

My only complaint is that the magnets are not super strong. Sometimes moving my laptop on the desk is enough to lose the connection.
text_fidelity_b: ZRSE Magnetic USB C Adapter, (2 Pack) USB C Magnetic Adapter, 24 Pins USB3.1 10Gbps Data Transfer 4K 60Hz Video PD 100w Charge Compatible with MacBook Pro/Air, Tablets&USB-C Devices

UBOTIE Bluetooth Wireless Keyboards, Colorful Cute Cat Deisgn Office Keyboards, Portable Slim Compact Size for Laptop, Tablet, Smart Phones(Purple-Colorful) This is a fairly standard wireless keyboard, with a very cute design element to make it more fun than your everyday utility keyboard.
The size is good, about 14"x6". A decent amount for most folks, still small enough to toss into a backpack or messenger bag and take with you.

It works as expected, and it was very nice to have a cleaning brush included- the stickers are a fun bonus and will probably appeal to some folks more than others.

I like the feel of this keyboard, not quite as "CLACK"-ish as some, but a good sound and feel nonetheless. It's pretty lightweight as well.

And clearly, it's cute. Very cute. The extra touch of the "inner ear" color on the left upper side is so nice. Tenergy TN480U 8-Bay LCD Display Fast Charger for NiMH/NiCD AA AAA Rechargeable Batteries with 4pcs 2500mah AA and 4pcs 1000mah AAA Rechargeable Batteries The charger comes with 8 AA rechargeable batteries, but not a power supply. Any USB power supply that can provide 1 to 2 amps of current will do. It comes with two cords -- a standard micro USB cord and a type C cord. Either will work to supply power to the charger.

You don't need to charge batteries in pairs with this charger. You can charge any number up to eight at a time. However, the instructions say that a 1 amp power supply is good for charging only up to four batteries, while charging eight requires a 2 amp power supply.

The display is bright and easy to see from even low angles. The display indicates which batteries are still charging, and which are full. The display has a basic progress meter in the form of the number of five bars representing each battery that remain lit as the batteries charge.

As far as the included batteries go, I own several Tenergy batteries already, and they've performed well. I expect these will do the same.
text_fidelity_b: Tenergy TN480U 8-Bay LCD Display Fast Charger for NiMH/NiCD AA AAA Rechargeable Batteries with 4pcs 2500mah AA and 4pcs 1000mah AAA Rechargeable Batteries

SOL REPUBLIC Deck Ultra Wireless Speaker with Outdoor Loudness Boost and Heist Mode Gunmetal, 1530-00 The SOL Republic is an impressive little speaker and the cut-to-the-chase is I'd strongly and happily recommend it. But a few specifics:

Packaging: Easily unpackaged, not too excessive

Charging: Mine came nearly fully charged. From whatever point it was at, it took about 7 or 8 minutes to reach full charge. I'll update with how long the charge lasts and how long to charge an empty battery once I get to that point

Pairing: Couldn't be easier, simpler, or faster. Turned it one, went to my bluetooth on my IOS devices (sorry, that's all I have so can't say what the Android experience is), and there it was. Worked seamlessly and immediately with all my devices and my laptop, both single-user mode and multi-party mode. Everything should pair so easily. Range was excellent--was bale to use it from every room on the same floor (didn't check it between floors)

Footprint/build: it's small (you can see the dimensions) and very light. But it delivers surprisingly solid sound with no distortion at the top volume and it feels nicely sturdy and solid despite its lack of real heft. Its sturdiness combined with its material makes me worry-free with regard to how it would hold up being moved around a room or transported from place to place.

sound: as mentioned, surprisingly full. I was really pleased with the volume, the clarity, and the richness of sound.

operation: again, couldn't be simpler. Two clearly marked volume buttons on the top-- + and -. The central bottom button performs several actions depending on if you hold it (change from "indoor" sound to "outdoor" sound) or tap it once or twice.

It connects via bluetooth, NFC, or line-in

In multiplayer mode, you can connect up to five devices and whoever hits play gets to play their music. Worked without a hitch with all five devices I hooked up. I can see this getting a lot of fun use.

Really, a nice piece of tech--good build quality, excellent sound, super ease of use, fun to use. So far it looks like they nailed everything (just waiting to see about the battery life and charging)
text_fidelity_b: SOL REPUBLIC Deck Ultra Wireless Speaker with Outdoor Loudness Boost and Heist Mode Gunmetal, 1530-00

Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers For years, I used the keyboard kindle after it first came out and loved the "classic" look of the page so much. After replacing it several times due to screen issues, I finally made the switch to the paperwhite with some skepticism, thinking the back-light would make it into yet another screen I look at. I was pleasantly surprised that even the brighter settings still look like a page, and I can turn it all the way down for the same effect as my older model kindle. Plus, I don't need to bother anyone with a light anymore when I read in bed, in the car at night, etc.

Paying a bit extra for no ads was worth it, and I enjoy the drawings that serve as screensavers. The home page is not my favorite - I would prefer to default to my library list instead of wading through recommendations, etc. - but it's not that much of a hassle to tap over to the library screen. When I'm reading a book, it automatically opens to the page I left off on just like my old kindle.

I only vaguely miss having the 3G function my old kindle had because I used to live out in the boonies with limited internet access. However, the WiFi has been generally sufficient and now I just make sure I download a few books before I travel.

Overall, the kindle has definitely revolutionized the way I read since it first came out when I was in high school. I do still keep a lot of hard copies of my favorite series and enjoy reading real books from time to time, but the kindle is SO easy to download anything, anytime you want. Not to mention bringing a whole library with you in one slim package while traveling! I have had this model for a year and a half now, and have no issues or complaints at this time.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers

Amazfit BIP smartwatch by Huami with all-day heart rate & activity tracking, sleep monitoring, GPS, 30-day battery life, Bluetooth (Kokoda Green), One Size June 7, 2018—This watch, an Amazfit Bip smartwatch, arrived today so I'm posting an initial review about it. I come back after some time and change or add anything that needs it.
----------------------------------
Amended June 15, 2018
I have downgraded the Amazfit Bip Smartwatch from 5-Stars to 1-Star. This is why:
1) My Pixel 2 updated to Android 8.1, the watch unpaired in the process and now will not reconnect (pair with) the phone.
2) Nothing in Amazfit's on-line support addresses this issue. However, there are a significant number of Bip owners discussing this problem on the internet, outside of Amazfit's site.
3) The watch is not a useless brick and exchanging texts with Amazfit's tech support is not going to get this fixed (if at all) in a timely enough manner for my purposes.
4) Finally, I got 7 1/2 days service from this watch and that is very poor, indeed.

Sorry to say, my opinion is the Bip does NOT WORK WITH ANDROID 8.1. That seemingly the case, what will happen when Android P, now in Beta, releases as Android 9 in August, 2018?

I'm going back to my iPhone/Apple Watch. Yes, that combination has glitches as well. However, support for Apple Products is always reliable and you're not stuck texting for help.

Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory Recording my listening experience with the Sennheiser HD 598 which I bought after breaking my pair of HE-400 headphones. I own Grado Labs SR80, BModed Fostex T50, Sennheiser HD-600, Hifiman HE-500.

Hour 1:
Pro: Looks good for plastic and reasonably comfortable.
Con: heavy handed, muddy, base reminds me of a one-note subwoofer, and the signature reminds me of a cheap pair of Skullcandy headphones. You could get better sound from a pair of Beat headphones. I am feeling ripped off and don't recall the last time listening to music made me MAD!
One word: Garbage!

Hour 10:
The headphones have opened up some. Vocals feel recessed. Bass still feels one dimensional. Upgraded rating from one to two stars.

Hour 15:
I am baffled by the positive reviews of this product. Yes, headphones and their sound signatures are very much a personal preference, but these are so grossly bad that I can only assume my ears are damaged or the headphones are defective. Returning them to Amazon.

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR WiFi Mesh Range Extender EX6400 - Coverage up to 2100 sq.ft. and 35 devices with AC1900 Dual Band Wireless Signal Booster & Repeater (up to 1900Mbps speed), plus Mesh Smart Roaming Works well if you can figure it out

I bought a Netgear EX6250 in a brick-and-mortar store about four months ago and my experience with it has been good overall...though not without its complications. Past experience with late-model Netgear products can be helpful in getting this unit set up and operating as the process is not always straightforward. It took me (who has a lot of experience with Netgear products and home networking in general) rather a few tries to get onto the right track in the Nighthawk app to set the thing up - you can run into roadblocks due to aspects of the Nighthawk app's design being less than intuitive (I know I did). I can't remember specifics now...so you know what I'm going to do? Out of lovingfriendliness for my fellow Amazon customers, I'm going to reset the extender to factory settings and set it back up, taking notes along the way, so that I can relate my experience more clearly and in greater detail.

Okay, so:

First you want to jump online and download the Netgear Nighthawk app to your phone. I don’t know if this unit can be set up without it.

Next, plug the extender into power - somewhere where it’s in range of your router. After you first plug the unit in, or after resetting it using the little recessed paperclip button on the side, the power LED will glow orange for rather a long time - two to three minutes in my experience - before finally turning green. Green means “go” - but orange doesn’t. So you just have to wait until that light turns green in order to be able to proceed with the setup process. Good opportunity to focus on the breath. And the fact that patience is a virtue.

Once the power indicator turns green, launch the Nighthawk app and check the little circle confirming that you accept Netgear’s terms and conditions and that you’ve read their privacy policy…even though you probably haven’t. Then tap “I Agree”.

On an iPhone, at least, the next screen says that iOS requires that you enable local network access in order to be able to set up your extender (which at this point the Nighthawk app is calling a “router” because it doesn’t yet know any better - you haven’t yet told it what you want to set up). Obviously, since you want to set up your extender, you’re going to okay that local network access. Tap “Continue” and your phone will ask you if you want to allow the app to find and connect to devices on your local network. Tap “OK”.

The next screen asks you to allow push notifications. This one’s up to you. I think I’ve always allowed them and I haven’t seen one yet, let alone been annoyed by excessive/unwanted notifications that are, in the end, just trying to sell me crap or otherwise waste my time.

The next screen tells you Netgear needs access to your device’s location services to automatically connect to your wifi network. I always allow this.

Next you’re told you have to create a new Netgear account or log into an existing one. Do that.

Then you’ll be asked if you want to enable Face ID and you’ll also be asked…something else I forget because I just blazed past it, momentarily forgetting that I was writing this detailed description of the process. But…y’know. You can read (because you’re reading this), so…tap the things on your screen that accord with your wishes. :)

At last we come to a screen that says, “Let’s set up your Nighthawk”, and tells you what to do if the unit’s been set up before. I don’t think I’ve ever had any luck using the “been set up before” option, so I always reset the extender to factory settings (by pressing and holding the paperclip/pen-point button on the side of the unit until the power light blinks orange) when I have a problem with the connection (which I seldom do, and when I do it’s usually because the power’s blinked or something else explicit has happened to make me need to set the extender up again). If this is your first time setting it up, tap “Set up a Nighthawk”. Even though I don’t think this extender is technically a Nighthawk. Doesn’t matter - you can still set it up with this app.

Next you’re shown a rundown of what’s going to happen. Read that as you’re inclined, then tap “Get Started!”.

On the product selection screen that comes up next, tap “Range Extender”.

The app tells you where to plug in your extender. Follow its instructions and tap “Next”.

The next screen just tells you to actually plug it in now, and wait (…and wait…and wait…) for a solid (green) power LED. Do that, and when you’ve got the solid green power light, tap “Next”.

On the next screen, the app will ask you to let it join your extender’s network. Tap “OK”, and wait while your phone connects to your extender. When it does, the screen will change to display “Great, we found your extender”. Tap “Next”.

Tap “Next” on the next screen as well.

Now your phone will look for your router’s network (which is your pre-existing wifi network, the one you want to extend). I think what it’s doing now is acting as a liaison between your router and the extender - introducing them to one another, as it were. Because what happens next is that your extender looks for and - ideally - connects to your wifi network. (When you’re asked to allow…something…to join your network, tap “Join”.)

And if all has gone well, that’s pretty much it. You’ll see a screen that says you’re up and running, and…there it is: you’re up and running!

Obviously, all of that is how things are *supposed* to go. If they go otherwise…you’ll probably need to be able to apply a searing laser beam of logic to the process and figure out how to make it work (that’s been my personal approach and, lucky for me, it’s always worked so far), or else to contact the dread Netgear Support People. I hope for your sake the laser beam works.

Good luck and enjoy!
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR WiFi Mesh Range Extender EX6400 - Coverage up to 2100 sq.ft. and 35 devices with AC1900 Dual Band Wireless Signal Booster & Repeater (up to 1900Mbps speed), plus Mesh Smart Roaming

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic HomeHawk Outdoor Wireless Smart Home Security Camera, Wide Angle View, Color Night Vision, 2-Way Talk, Works with Alexa & Google Assistant, 1 Camera Kit (KX-HN7001W) The Panasonic HomeHawk system has its good and its areas that could use some upgrades.
The good:
This is about as simple and install as you will get for a home monitoring system. No wires, five screws, charging the camera, downloading the app and you are ready to go, it is that simple. Once the cameras are charged and mounted I think it took me about 5 minutes to get everything running, and I am not technical by any stretch of the imagination.
The cameras are clear and provide good picture (you can select the quality of the picture when setting the system up) of the areas they are monitoring. Recordings are of good quality and clear, the night recording can be either color or black and white (infrared) depending on your choice.
Recording trigger areas can be set up along with sensitivity to movement in the recording area to trigger the recording to begin. All of these are very handy and easy to use.
The app is simple to use and pretty intuitive on how the system operates allowing almost everyone to use the system without any special knowledge. In all a good system for 95% of the people out there.
The things that can be improved.
It became apparent during setup of the outdoor camera (the one that looks like ET) that you need to mount it in a specific orientation, if you turn it over you cannot flip the image and everything will be upside down. If the ball neck for mounting the camera was just a little longer this would not be an issue as you could fit it under a soffit on your house wit a large field of view.
On the outdoor camera it works best when the rear of the camera is pointed in the direction of the base unit for connectivity. As you turn the camera and point the rear away from the base the signal drops pretty quick and the camera will not connect.
Other than these items the system is pretty easy to set up and use, now we see all the raccoons that show up to the house at night.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic HomeHawk Outdoor Wireless Smart Home Security Camera, Wide Angle View, Color Night Vision, 2-Way Talk, Works with Alexa & Google Assistant, 1 Camera Kit (KX-HN7001W)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech MX Master 3S for Mac Wireless Bluetooth Mouse, Ultra-Fast Scrolling, Ergo, 8K DPI, Quiet Clicks, Track on Glass, USB-C, Apple, iPad - Space Grey - With Free Adobe Creative Cloud Subscription I’m really picky when it comes to mice. I usually end up with a gaming mouse because they are comfortable and fulfill my needs. But because I use a Mac, it’s rare that I can customize buttons and macros and all that.

So I was really excited to try out the Logitech MX Master 3. I’ve been using it for the past month and keep going back to it. I have two work spaces in my house, and I find myself taking the mouse from desk to desk, instead of using what’s already on the desk.

The mouse feels nice in my hand. I have small hands (size small in gloves), and the mouse nestles nicely against my palm. My fingers don’t have to stretch to reach any of the buttons. The thumb rest is comfortable. I only wish the mouse had better pinky support.

The scroll wheel … I love the scroll wheel. Logitech calls it the “MagSpeed™ Electromagnetic” scroll wheel which is a really fancy way of saying it scrolls like butter. The wheel is nearly silent and super precise. It has just the right amount of feedback when scrolling slowly through a page, and flies when I want to get to the bottom of a long article. It really is a joy to use.

The mouse charges via USB-C and includes a USB-C to USB-C cable. I couldn’t try out the Flow option, where you can copy/paste text, images, and files between computers because my other Mac’s version of iOS is too old to install Logitech Options. But I was able to connect the mouse to both of my Macs and switch between them using the 1, 2, 3 button on the bottom.

Logitech Options offers a decent amount of customization. You can customize settings across all applications, such as pointer and scrolling speed. Some of the buttons can be customized: gesture, scroll wheel click, wheel shift, horizontal scroll, back, and forward.

App specific options can be assigned to the buttons. Defaults are assigned for the most popular programs like Chrome and Photoshop, and I was able to add customizations for my personal favorite, Scrivener.

But what I don’t like is that I’m limited in picking what the buttons can do. I really wanted to change the horizontal scroll wheel into another vertical scroll wheel, but I can’t. I can only do the functions Logitech thinks I want, such as zooming or navigating between tabs.

The MX Master 3 has a lot of nice functions and has been designed for productivity. I’ve barely touched on a lot of what you can do with this mouse.

I just wish I could customize *everything* because what I need for productivity doesn’t match what someone else needs, or what Logitech assumes I want.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech MX Master 3S for Mac Wireless Bluetooth Mouse, Ultra-Fast Scrolling, Ergo, 8K DPI, Quiet Clicks, Track on Glass, USB-C, Apple, iPad - Space Grey - With Free Adobe Creative Cloud Subscription

text_fidelity_a:
Click 'n Dig Model E4 Key Finder. 4 Receivers. Wireless RF Remote Item, Wallet Locator Okay, this is an update to the one-star review I emitted originally. The Click 'n' Dig folks are definitely getting their money's worth from their PR people, whom I would hire myself if I could afford to hire someone who works that hard. After viewing my crabby review (below), they got in touch and offered to send a new set (you get the key finder and several other pieces that you can attach to other easily lost items). Surely, said they, the set shipped to me must have been defective. Would I take another one and if it improved, would I consider re-reviewing?

Oh, why not? I have nothing else to do during the hours left around the seven 14-hour days a week entailed in running a business. :-D They sent the doodads in the mail.

MEANWHILE... Between the time I first posted my original grutch and the time the new package of goodies arrived, I lost my keys not once, not twice, but THREE TIMES.

Each time, the Key Finder located the things! Inside a purse...on a piece of furniture where I'd dropped the keys to rescue the dog...atop a countertop where no one in their right mind would ever leave their keys...

It's not a matter of standing wherever you happen to be and clicking the "finder" device. You do have to walk around the house, and you do have to point the finder in several directions until it locates and connects with the receiver on your keyring. Its signal will pass through some but not all walls (why, I do not know: possibly electrical wiring or insulation?). Its range is about 20 feet, I'd guess. It requires some patience and persistence on your part, but it does eventually work.

Click 'n' Dig sent me a new set, which I gave to some dear friends who are even more superannuated than I after the Missus expressed dismay at having lost her keys once again. This is one of those tools that makes old age tolerable...maybe even survivable.

***********

ORIGINAL WHINGE: Not sending this back, because I don't have time to hassle with repackaging and mailing. But can't recommend it. These devices are supposed to emit a 90-decibel beep when you point the hand-held radio transmitter at them. Thus if you have one on, say, a key ring, you should be able to locate the keys if you misplace them around the house. We're told the radio frequency goes through walls and has an 80-foot range.

Well, if that's 90 decibels, then 90 decibels isn't very loud. According to Purdue University, 90 db is as loud as a "Boeing 737 or DC-9 aircraft at one nautical mile (6080 ft) before landing (97 dB); power mower (96 dB); motorcycle at 25 ft (90 dB). Newspaper press (97 dB)." Dang! I wish!! If aircraft made the same level of sound as this handy-dandy beeper, the skies would be a lot quieter around here!! :-D And my neighbor's Harley would be a lot more fun, too...

No, the signal does not go through walls.

The range is about 25 feet. Any further away than that, and the transmitter will not elicit a beep. If your keys have dropped out of your pocket and slipped under a chair cushion, you have to be right on top of the chair to get receiver to beep.

Could be the gadgets need new batteries, which are kindly included. But the instructions do not show how to find the battery cases or how to open them. On the key fob, it's obvious enough where the battery case is, but you can't get it open -- I split a fingernail and hurt my finger when I tried. On the flat gadgets that you can stick to objects with the provided double-sided tape, I can't even find a CLUE to where a battery case could be opened. ?????????

The idea behind this device is truly brilliant. Sure do wish the execution were better.
text_fidelity_b: Click 'n Dig Model E4 Key Finder. 4 Receivers. Wireless RF Remote Item, Wallet Locator

I have the kindle keyboard ereaders 1st and 3rd gen , the 2nd gen Fire 8.9" and last year I bought the 6" Fire. I would not have bought this one except that my 6" Fire has gotten glitchy. I have not had problems with any of my kindles before so I chalked it up to just a bad egg.
I was thinking of replacing it when I found this great deal on the lastest 7" Fire. $100 for a tablet is such a deal. $50 is AMAZING!!

Garmin Forerunner 910XT GPS Multisport Watch with Heart Rate Monitor - Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer) As many have already written this watch has software issues. It does not display pace accurately. There's absolutely NO EXCUSE for Garmin releasing a training watch that doesn't know a person's pace. That's the sole reason this is getting a one star rating. On top of this, it is a simple software fix that they have still failed to make.

There is a simple work around: don't display pace and instead display lap pace. Lap pace has no issues and accurately describes your current pace. All the other pace features also work. Lap pace, ave pace, last lap pace are all accurate. The fact that everything else works fine shows to me it is just a software issue that Garmin could pretty easily fix if they bothered to spend 10 minutes on the issue. I probably would have given it four stars without this issue.

Why I really, really like this watch:

I bought this to supplement/replace my 405CX

The display is bigger and better. You can display four metrics at a time across four screens - so 16 metrics. The font is BOLD and easy to see even in tough conditions. While working out, you can hit the down or up arrow to more quickly get the screen you want to see. Also, even at its smallest, the font is bold and readable even to old eyes that don't see up close so well. The font describing each display is too small for my eyes to see when I have contacts in. So, I need to memorize which spot displays what. Still, this is sooo much better than the 405CX. On that watch, I can only see the big middle display with my contacts in.

The watch vibrates alerts. This is awesome!! I hate watches beeping at me and in loud conditions I would miss the beeps. I much prefer the vibration and I just turn off the audio alerts altogether. Also, the watch now alerts you (via beep or vibrate or both or none - your choice) when it has a GPS lock. The 405 never did this. Awesome improvement.

The battery lasts forever. Well probably not forever but you can use it for an entire day with GPS. The manual claims 22 hrs - I've yet to use it up when I started fully charged. The 405 claimed 8 hrs but it was really more like 6. Also, the 910 can be turned off so you can NOT waste the battery during travel time to your work out starting point.

It shows your recovery heart rate about one minute after you push 'stop' if you don't do the reset count downtime. Someone else mentioned that here. It a wonderful feature and not mentioned at all in the promotional material or users manual.

No touch bezel. The touch bezel in the 405 and 510 is a miserable feature. It has a life of its own in humid conditions which pretty much describes most of the heavily populated USA during most of the months of the year folks train a lot outside. The 910 completely relies on pushing buttons so now it only does things when you WANT the watch to do something. Also, the start/stop/lap/reset buttons are on the face of the watch. Everything else is on the sides. This keeps me from accidently hitting the wrong button when I don't mean to.

GPS programming seems smarter than the 405 / 510. With the 405 or 510 if you stop your movement and forget to hit stop on the watch it will keep adding distance. (For example, you can sit on a bench for a 15 minute break and it will add 0.5 miles to your distance.) I think this is because of GPS not knowing your exact location so it keeps seeing you as 10-20 feet from the last place it thought you were and keeps adding this up even though you are not moving. The 910 seems to do a lot less of this. It's still adds a bit of distance but over a 15 minute break it might be 0.05 miles instead of 0.5 miles.

Other things to note:

This watch is NOT smaller than other Garmin watches but it does stick out from your wrist less but to make up for that it is wider and taller. My guess is that it weighs pretty much the same. If you have a tiny wrist like mine, it can actually be a bit too big for your wrist. I got the cloth strap - this makes that issue much better.

I have not used it for swimming and I don't think I'm going to. It's not worth the risk if there is even a chance of screen fogging.

The manual not very useful. It doesn't show all the features. It is close to unintelligible. If I hadn't already had the 405 and was sorta familiar with how Garmin watches were organized, I'm not sure if I could have figured this out. Garmin's online help is no better.

Hint for female users: I skipped the heart rate monitor that came with the watch and instead got the original plastic hr monitor. I take off the strap and just place the main plastic part inside to top of my bra. It works great this way and is much more comfortable than having a strap wrapped around me and much easier to get in and out of and you don't have to find a private place to do it. I'm not sure if this will work for all women but it might be worth trying if you hate have a bra, HR monitor strap, plus shirt all binding around you like I do.

ETA 04-Jun-2012

I have found that lap pace isn't accurate either. Very disappointing. My latest work around is to reduce by lap distance to 0.25 miles. Last lap pace is accurate so by setting my laps as a very short distance, I'm getting constant feedback on my pace. Still, I think for a serious training regime, this wouldn't work. It's close enough for me.

(When I say not accurate, I mean not remotely accurate. It will show my pace as 10 minutes slower than I am going and it will stay that way for a full lap. Only when the lap is complete - it then shows total time for the lap correctly. It's not 5 minutes fast for half the time and 5 minutes slow for half the time. It's just off all the time and usually shows me as going at a pace 5-10 minutes slower than I am actually moving.)

On the a positive: another feature I'm really, really liking is the ability to manually scroll through the metric screens. I now set the screens to not scroll at all. I just use the up and down button and they get me to any screen I need. It's very nice for when all I care about is say, my heart rate. I just leave it on my HR screen but if I happen want to know my distance, then I can scroll to that screen and then back to my HR screen.

I'm also really, really still loving the giant display numbers. I can read these in any conditions. Rain, darkness, poor light, as I'm moving fast and don't have time to hold my hand still, etc.

ETA 09-Sep-2012
Garmin's support website has a post from 16-Aug-2012 that claims to have fixed the pace issue with a firmware update. I'm downloading it now. I'm planning an 11 mile hike today. I will post again if this fixes the issue.

See Garmin's site > tech support > search on 910 > search on 'pace issues.' Sorry, amazon removed the url.

BTW - I'm still using the 910 over the 405 despite the pace issue. The display and button functionality/placement of the 910 is just so superior to the 405 that it's worth the pace problems. I took my lap distance down to 0.10 miles so I get near continuous feedback on my pace that way.

Update 10-Sep-2012
The pace issue does seemed to be fixed!!! Or least, highly improved. The pace keeps nice and steady. It takes a few seconds of a changed pace for the watch to pick up on it which seems totally reasonable. Clearly there needs to be a lot of smoothing for the math equations seeing as GPS accuracy is only 15-20 feet and it only takes a reading every few seconds. Downloading the update is odd and I wasn't 100% sure it took but it does seem to have. My watch now displays my version as 2.6.

Upping my stars to five.

Update 07-July-2013.

With much trepidation, I just starting using this for open water swims. I've only done two so far in fresh water lakes. No fogging. Distances seem accurate enough. Maps show it has me within 30-40 meters of my real location. So far so good. I have not tried it in a pool.

I've also started using it on a bike. Just on my wrist. Lots of fun seeing how fast I'm going, etc but have yet to use it for any disciplined training. Just starting out but I really like it for this so far.

Also - Pace issue still seems fixed. It isn't as good as the old 405 but it also doesn't eat battery strength like the 405 did. I'll take the trade off.

Update 23-Dec-2014
I continue to heavily use this. Now the light has stopped working. It's past its warranty now. I'm reluctant to send it in to get fixed because I'm in training and don't want to be without it. It can be hard sometimes to get the charger attached these days. The attach points are extremely well worn at this point. I've used it 20+ time for swimming and have had no issues with fogging like some others have reported.

text_fidelity_a:
Schlage WCE100 Home Indoor Camera with Nexia Home Intelligence, White This is the best overview of the components I've seen so far:

Nexia Home Bridge (this is the key component)
Schlage touch screen deadbolt w alarm
Schlage home keypad lock
Schlage home dimmer/appliance module
Schlage home indoor camera
Schlage home outdoor camera
Trane home energy management thermostat
American Standard AccuLink((tm)) remote thermostat
Trane ComfortLink ((tm)) II Control
American Standard AccuLink((tm)) Platinum ZV control (?)
Schlage home door/window sensor
Schlage home motion sensor
Other Z-Wave sensor
Other Z-Wave thermostat
Other Z-Wave lighting device
Other Z-Wave wall switch and outlet

They might have considered making the 9V battery compartment in the "Bridge" just a little bit bigger. It's a mighty snug fit and you have to remove the battery to get the MAC ID. In fact, you have to remove the 9V battery so often it's a curiosity why the battery door is such a pain to remove and why the battery is so difficult to get out of its little bay. I was actually using a flat screwdriver to pry the battery out, it's that tight.

---

Overall, now that the camera, light dimmer and lock and installed, "enrolled" and apparently functional..? WHAT A GREAT SYSTEM!!! The components look great, they're top-quality. Now that I see everything in action (especially video of my home on my iPhone) the subscription fee seems like not such a high price to pay for what you're getting. I know that I'm going to be sorely tempted to add more cameras.

The deadbolt operates with a passcode OR with a physical key. At first I was thinking that you could lock yourself out accidentally but after examining the lock and playing with the buttons I see that is not the case.

I also understand why the light dimmer module goes so well with the indoor camera -- when it gets dark, you'd want to be able to ramp up the light enough for the camera to see! It's a temptation to put the indoor camera in one of my kids room, which is what I might have done when they were small. That would be a rude intrusion these days. So it's outside a hallway that all traffic must pass through. The field of vision nearly covers the two main doors into and out of our home, also. So I can keep an eye on who's getting home when and all that parent-of-teenagers type stuff.

Is there a controller for exterior lights? Or some kind of interface that would allow me to remotely control wired exterior lights?

The only downside to this system, aside from the kludge-y installation process, is that you will want to add more components, and they aren't cheap.

Bottom line: top-quality components, frustrating "enrollment" process -- once you get it all up and running, it's quite impressive. It's nearly worth the frustration to see it all in operation. It would be nice if you could pan-and-zoom the camera. Perhaps that will be forthcoming in another camera model.

I can't help but feel that the process of "enrolling" the components couldn't be made more simple or more streamlined.

Now to budget for an exterior camera... maybe two...

---

Now that I've seen the system in operation I grasp what the manufacturer is actually offering -- remote control of your home administered via your iPhone or iPad. Ideal for working professionals. Getting everything connected and communicating was a little effort, but it's really a beautiful system in operation. You will definitely want to add more light controls and cameras, at least I would. I wonder if there's an exterior light module? There must be. Once you see it in operation the subscription will not be an issue. You are getting more than what you're paying for.

An excellent upgrade to your home and a clever way to keep tabs on a vacation home.
text_fidelity_b: Schlage WCE100 Home Indoor Camera with Nexia Home Intelligence, White

Lepow Portable Monitor - 2023 C2 15.6 inch FHD 1080P Portable Display with IPS Screen, Foldable Kickstand, Dual Speakers, Type-C HDMI Mini DP Port for Laptop PC Phone Xbox Switch PS5, Iron Gray First off I was a little irate with this product. I was so excited when it arrived today, that I was tracking Amazon. Okay upon opening this monitor the packaging was done right. Everything you need is in the box.

I am a coder and I needed this monitor to work perfectly with my Macbook Pro 2020 version.
This is from my experience others may have not experiences the trails and frustration I dealt with. I was seriously debating on returning it to the UPS store.
I couldn't get the picture to work. I worked on it for about 30 minutes and started surfing the web. I came across a video and watched this guy plug it in on the left side and it worked. So it will help to read and look at the pictures in the booklet first.

To save you the hours of frustration I experienced with this product, I will give you the information you need for this to work minutes out of the box. If you want to read this instead of the book.

1. Plug the USB-C port into the left side of the monitor. (I did all the other ports except that one.)

2. Plug into your USB-C port and the picture will work. No stand by or black-outs unless you use all the other ports besides the one on the left.

3. Issue: How do you have more than one thing on the screen?
System preferences>display>arrangement (important!)
The white box in the arrangement tab above the box, that is your Macbook. The second box is your monitor. If you want the monitor on the right side, move the box without the white bar over to the right. The same goes for the left. Now drag that picture over to the side your monitor is on and Bam!!! Beauty!

4. Problem: You don't want to use the volume on the monitor you'd rather listen on your Macbook.
System preferences>sound>output>slide that over to MacBook Pro speakers and take it off that Z1 crap. (That took me a while too.)
Overall, after the stress and migraine, I endured trying to figure this product out. I will have to say it works perfectly for my needs for now.
You better bet your bottom dollar if I have one issue with this product I will be returning it ASAP! Spending more than a hundred dollars on any product during COVID 19 is too much.

Overall I am glad I made this purchase and I'm glad I didn't take it to the UPS store to return it.
text_fidelity_b: Lepow Portable Monitor - 2023 C2 15.6 inch FHD 1080P Portable Display with IPS Screen, Foldable Kickstand, Dual Speakers, Type-C HDMI Mini DP Port for Laptop PC Phone Xbox Switch PS5, Iron Gray

Anyway, it's a ton of fun, and it's got me drawing stuff again.

Philips DVT5000/00 4 GB Digital Voice Tracer with 3 Built-in Microphones Voice Recorder This is a good voice recorder. Whether you need it to record your voice memos, lectures, meetings, or discretely record your favorite spy, this will surely be a recorder you'll find many uses for.

It feels very secure in your hand, and has a comfortable feel and weight. It comes with a small pouch, which is nice. The record button is easy to find my sight or feel. The volume and forward/reverse buttons are on an outer button from the record button. Play and stop on the left and index and menu are on the right.

f1 and f2 buttons are primarily used for setting mic sensitivity and voice quality. Under Mic Sensitivity you can choose: Dictate (good for personal memos), Speech recognition (turns on when it hears voice), conversation (good for interviews or conversations, auto zoom (good for large areas where there may be close up voices and far voices), and lecture (good for lectures)

You can choose either low quality at 8kbps in Mp3 format to super high quality 192kbps in mp3. There is also a wave format in 1411 kbps. The higher quality you go impacts total record time. You can add a micro SD card for adding recording time.

There are also 4 index folders labeled A thru D. These are for separating projects. There is also a folder you could place music files if you wanted this to be a mp3 player.

There is also a menu setting where the voice quality and mic sensitivity can be accessed as well as numerous other options such as splitting files, display contrast, and clearvoice (an option that improves the sound quality of the recorded voiec)

The unit comes with rechargable AA batteries that will need to be charged when you first open it. They charge with the included usb to micro USB cord. Any other micro USB cord you own will also work. Once the recorder is connected to your computer through the USB cable you can download and upload voice or mp3 and wave files.

The only thing I wish this had was different settings for each index. For instance I would have liked to set index A for lecture mode at high quality, index B for dictate at a lower quality, etc. Once you set a mic sensitivity and recording quality, they are the same for all index until you change them in settings.

Overall a great quality recorder. Great for meetings, memos, and conversations.
text_fidelity_b: Philips DVT5000/00 4 GB Digital Voice Tracer with 3 Built-in Microphones Voice Recorder

text_fidelity_a:
Tile - (Gen 1) - 1 Pack - Discontinued by Manufacturer The Tile system isn't perfect but it works (mostly) and to date I haven't run across any better options. So bearing in mind your needs and the device's limitations, it's probably worth getting (at the time of this writing) if you have things you're worried about misplacing.

Pros:

- EASY setup. The time it takes to send an eMail and receive a reply, and a few seconds more. I have heard people say it requires iPhone 4 and up - I have a 5 and everything was a breeze. I didn't use the picture feature initially but it was no problem to update later.

- Decent map feature - good enough to get you in general range of the FIND radius.

- An audible FIND jingle. Just loud enough to hear through a wallet. Louder sure would be better, but it has a tinny high-pitched jingle that's easy to identify once you've heard it.

- It's small enough to fit in my wallet. It's a bit bulky, but it does.

- It's weatherproof and sealed. I haven't actually tested that and don't want to, but it's a nice feature.

- On-phone settings are easy to operate, and allow you to turn off Bluetooth tracking without turning off the iPhone's Bluetooth.

- Easy to assign to other objects as needed (if you don't use the stick pad.) It has a hole, so you don't HAVE to stick it to anything permanently.

- Can add other users (beforehand, of course!)

- It works. The battery is only supposed to last about a year, though (we'll see!)

Cons:

- Bulkier than I thought - not quite as thick as a pen, but almost. About a half-dollar size.

- The FIND process takes a minute or two to adjust and is a little confusing at first.

- The FIND radius sure isn't perfectly accurate. But hey, it's something!

- Battery not replaceable. The Tile people will recycle it for you for a fee, but I doubt that is a rapid process.

I really like it. I don't lose stuff that often, but this is an awfully convenient tracking option - having a general idea is a LOT better than having NO idea at all! And I LOVE the idea of the Tile community! The Tile gives me peace of mind taking things through airports etc. If there's something you think you MIGHT mislay, I think the Tile is worth it.
text_fidelity_b: Tile - (Gen 1) - 1 Pack - Discontinued by Manufacturer

OontZ Angle 3 Bluetooth Speaker, Portable Wireless Bluetooth 5.0 Speaker, 10 Watts, Crystal Clear Stereo Sound, Rich Bass, IPX5 Water Resistant, Loud Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Black) I was very disappointed after reading so many positive reviews.

This unit was to be primarily used in my bathroom with my Iphone 6 while I get ready for work. It was to replace a JBL Charge I'd had for a few years and no longer would hold a charge.

The sound is strong, but tinny. No real depth or strong bass notes. I played several songs and really, really wanted it to work. Finally, I just gave up.

Now, the reason I gave it 2 stars is that it would be perfect for spoken-word use. It paired up fairly quick and the size is simply perfect for portability. And it is very attractive.

So I decided to give the Angle 3 Plus a shot for $7.00 more. Wow - what a difference! Sounds great, bass is perfect for the size, and I couldn't be happier.

Bottom line is that the choice is totally subjective on the part of the listener but, for the money, the Cambridge Angle 3 Plus is the way to go.

Unfortunately their customer service do not offer too much help.

Following you will find how they answered a question I submitted regarding the USB attached drives issue:

My question:
I have been trying to use Windows Backup with a drive attached via USB to this unit. I
have tried different hard drives formatted both as FAT32 and NTFS. Backups always
fail. Mostly with Error code: 0x80070008. Is there a compatibility issue between this
router and Windows Backup? I still have two weeks to return this router if I cannot
make it work.

Their response:
The router has its own settings that will operate reguardless if the computer works or not. The computer has nothing to do with the router software one way or the other. If you need to back up the router setting then I suggest you take screen shots of the router to verify that you can save the settings from there.
Thanks Aaron Asus Support Team

Well, I am still trying to figure out what their response means...

Do not get this router if you need USB features. They do not work.

Kindle Fire HDX 7", HDX Display, Wi-Fi and 4G LTE, 16 GB - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 3rd) I update to the latest Kindle every year. The HDX 7" is great with Wi-Fi. I like the 64 GB and quad core processor. The dual band wi-fi can use more power than my Internet can really deliver. I will probably have to update my whole Internet package. When I use the wi-fi to do downloads, everything on my wi-fi slows to a crawl and my Internet movies on Amazon and home computer freeze till it is done. I think my phone company only offers 100 Mbps with my current package. This kindle is powerful and takes over my whole Wi-Fi service.
The power adapter is a little different this year and goes in at an angle (thought it didn't fit). The adapter comes with the Kindle.
I will be keeping my old Kindle Fire HD, because I still enjoy it and some of the old apps I am not tired of yet (not compatible to HDX). I will be able to upload more of my pdf's to this newer Kindle, because pdf's use a lot more space. Also I can download more TV shows and movies, since I live in the Amazon ecosystem.
I like the clock on the screen is back. When I open the Kindle cover, the clock is in the corner with the date. That was not on the HD, but was on the first Fire (it was bigger).
I like the offers, because it is important to me what else is available. The screen is beautiful as always. I did have to make some adjustments to brightness (using settings) and the books (using view) I am reading. Actually for us older folks, brighter is better.
The sound is nice. I was watching PBS channel out in my yard and my neighbors could hear it. The PBS channel app was not something I was aware of before, but loving it now (even with my Internet service).
The HDX is smaller than the HD 7", but the screen is still the same size.
The camera on the 7"HDX is better than the HD. I really like it, because it comes with its own app, and I don't have to download a free app like last year. The one on my 7" HD has problems but was free.

text_fidelity_a:
Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red) I really hate to use the word “cute” but there’s no way around it – this is a cute cam! It looks pretty much the same as the original Cube, but offers improved video and the addition of WiFi. Of the new features, the WiFi is the most significant, and makes this far more useful as a cam.

I also have the original Cube and the build quality continues to be very good. These are priced higher than the “no name” action cams, but after using (and breaking) a couple of those, it’s nice to be able to count on the Cube to keep on working. It’s water resistant, which makes it less worrisome when using it in bad weather or around water. It supports up to a 128MB SD card

The form factor and overall design is much the same as the original Cube. It has a magnet in the base that is more than strong enough to keep it well-planted. It’s not strong enough for significant activity (e.g., staying on a bike handle while riding) but it offers the benefit of tripod-like stability without the need for a tripod (providing you have something metal to fasten the magnet).

The biggest change is wifi on the Cube+. I found the setup to be straightforward – basically just download the app and follow the setup steps. I love that the app lets you use it as a live view – that’s a big improvement over the original Cube. It’s a very helpful feature for planning a shot, plus allows me to monitor how things are turning out without having to play the video.

Image quality has been impressive – zero complaints there. I was pleased with the resolution of the original Cube, and this is a bit better. Audio quality is OK. It’s not outstanding, but it clearly picks up voices. I understand that earlier versions of the Cube+ had very poor sound quality, but the one I have (got it in Dec 2015) is fine with regard to sound.

All in all, it’s a great cam with a fun form factor and look. Well worth considering if you’re looking for a small profile action cam with solid build quality and performance. While the price has increased over that of the original Cube, the wifi features are very useful and well implemented, making this version well worth the additional cost.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red)

text_fidelity_a: Jensen CD-555 Pink CD Bluetooth Boombox Portable Bluetooth Music System with CD Player +CD-R/RW & FM Radio with Aux-in & Headphone Jack Line-in Limited Edition (Pink) I was looking for a portable CD player to use in my van which didn't come with one. I also wanted one that was simple to use and didn't have a lot of fancy features. I ordered a different player and wasn't happy with it and ended up returning it. Although this player had some negative reviews I thought I'd take my chances to see if I like this one. It isn't as portable as the smaller one I returned, but I'm extremely happy with it. It now sits on my kitchen counter and I listen to the local radio station every day and I wasn't even looking for a CD player with a radio feature. I haven't tried the bluetooth feature yet and not sure if I will. The radio and sound are great and you can really crank it up loud which I couldn't do with the first player I tried. I like the carry handle which makes it so easy to transport from room to room and the fact that it can be used with batteries. The only negatives I see with this CD player: (1) the size is a bit larger than I wanted but this enables it to have larger speakers and better sound quality doesn't it? (2) I would like it to be USB rechargeable instead of having to be plugged in and (3) the color claims to be red but it is more pink than red (when everything else I own is real red, this is a bit irritating). Overall, I am happy with this Jensen CD Player and will not be sending it back.
text_fidelity_b: Jensen CD-555 Pink CD Bluetooth Boombox Portable Bluetooth Music System with CD Player +CD-R/RW & FM Radio with Aux-in & Headphone Jack Line-in Limited Edition (Pink)

Now I get rid of all my trash and not let it build up wasting my battery.  I am surprised by how nice a droid this is and I only paid $39.00 for it.  I've paid much more for similar droids and they crashed and burned within a year or two.  I think this one will last a lot longer.  It comes with charging cord but it's too short to use if you're wanting to use the Kindle while it's charging, but it's nice to have as a spare cord. The screen has good clarity and nice touch response.  The sound quality is so-so but if I want to listen to music or watch a video I'll use earbuds. I really don't have any complaints about this Kindle Fire and I think it was $39.00 very well spent.  I just wish I had bought one a long time ago and saved myself several hundred dollars on the other droids that didn't last for very long or were too incredibly slow to even use.

text_fidelity_a:
jumper EZbook 3 Pro Windows 10 Laptop 13.3" FHD Bezel-Less, Intel Slim Ultrabook Portable, 6GB RAM 64GB ROM, Metal Shell Lightweight Notebook Update: I do really like this computer. It has smoothly integrated into my home network and I now quickly go to it for quick and easy browsing and/or controlling stuff in my house (particularly if the main computer is in use by somebody else or for some reason tethered. The great thing is that with the full power of Windows and third party software, it can be whatever you need it to be. The one negative I've found, though, is that the delete key is under the backspace key where you expect backslash to be (which is in turn beside the right alt key). For this reason, I've accidentally went into sleep mode a few times, which is annoying. You can turn off the power key (while running) in windows, but the delete key still isn't where it is supposed to be.

Original review:

Surprise! I actually love this computer.

I mean, I am a bit of a power user, so I have a big gaming laptop and a couple of servers throughout my house, not to mention a few purpose-built niche laptops. So while I was a bit skeptical of this machine before it came since I saw the low price tag, I think it's awesome for the right purpose.

I mean, I totally get what "Chrome Books" are trying to do - be low price, low weight computers that run basically "from the cloud". But who really wants a computer running Android? I mean, there are phones for that. So running Windows 10 is a great idea. (Not that I love Windows 10, but if you install Windows Classic Shell and tweak, tweak, tweak away...turn off all permissions, get rid of all the stupid crap they're trying to sell you, use an offline account, then it is almost as good as Windows 7).

Anyway, you don't get a lot of fancy new stuff, but what you do get is important: 1080p screen, mini-HDMI out (odd choice, would have gone for micro or even full, but whatever), 2 USB 3.0 (No C), a micro-SD card reader, headphone jack, and a M.2 expansion port.

64GB of ROM is pretty small, but they installed so little bloatware (just one program to make the touchpad better - I uninstalled it because I didn't recognize it, am paranoid, and figure I can adjust it with whatever is built into Windows) that you have ~45GB free. Should be enough for stuff like MS office and other junk you may want. But you know what, I have a 36TB NAS, and Windows works flawlessly with it, so if I'm using this as a home machine, it's not a problem. I don't much care for public cloud, so if I want to take this on the road, I can always stream (usually still reach my NAS) or just throw in an SSD (by the way, it only takes the small form factor) or a giant micro-SD card (although admittedly either of these factors takes away the fact that this item is inexpensive to begin with.

6GB of RAM is sufficient for a computer that is not meant to be a workhorse.

It's really thin and light and with a real keyboard is just delightful as opposed to dealing with a tablet; a tablet always disappoints me when I'm trying to get something done quickly. It also boots up fast due to NAND memory. It doesn't even look cheap or anything. It actually looks pretty good.

It has a regular "wall wart" type AC adapter instead of the usual laptop power brick. I like this, but the cord is a little short (on the other hand, it is likely easily replaced with something in my electronics closet) The barrel adapter goes into the right side of the device (which is not abnormal, but less normal than the back or the other side in my experience) and the unfortunate part is that it will partially fit into the stereo mini-plug port for headphones on the same spot on the other side, which is likely to cause some confusion.

The only apparent downside is that the keyboard seems...like it vibrates slightly. Like it's not held in tight enough or something. I mean, it does have nice keys and overall I like it, but it just feels slightly weird, although still much better than a tablet roll-out keyboard.

I actually really like this little machine. Not for my main computer or my only computer, but definitely for easy browsing, or a multimedia machine for a teen, or a school computer, a travel computer, whatever. I'd use it for plenty of things, happily.

If you're cool with the memory - and living off a NAS, an SD card, or the cloud - and you're looking for something small and usable, definitely give this some consideration.
text_fidelity_b: jumper EZbook 3 Pro Windows 10 Laptop 13.3" FHD Bezel-Less, Intel Slim Ultrabook Portable, 6GB RAM 64GB ROM, Metal Shell Lightweight Notebook

Even though it sits higher than my other tracker, I like that it looks like an every day stylish watch and not like a fitness tracker. And it's very comfortable to wear. The buttons on the sides are more low keyed and not that obvious that it is a fitness tracker.
Love the sleep tracker of this smartwatch. My other tracker wasn't as good as tracking my sleep.
Step tracking is right on track with what I am walking. Very important to me.
I am still learning all the nice functions that come with this Misfit. So far I love the call notification and the alerts. Like that I can play and pause my music without taking my phone out of my pocket. I am still working on learning how to work my home smart devices using the Misfit but, I know in time, and with practice, I will figure it all out. It's not hard, I've just been really busy with working and haven't had the time with working with all the fun functions.
I also love that I don't have to take it off and protect it if I'm out hiking and get caught in a rain storm. I'm out almost every weekend walking in some nature trail or another. So I get caught in a few unexpected downpours while I'm out.
Now some of the more difficult "to do's" with the Misfit...
Setting the time isn't impossible, just need a lot of patience.
Using a magnifying glass, and good light, helped me get the misfit logo centered in that itty bitty hole at the 6 oclock mark. Whewww...
The watch doesn't have a backlight. So it's so hard to see the time in low light, impossible in the dark.
I wish it was thinner than it is. I'm not used to wearing a watch, or a fitness tracker, that is as thick as this one is.
I don't like the color of the watch band that came with the rose gold colored watch. All the other colored watches comes with a matching band. This watch comes with more silver colored band and silver buckle. Just doesn't look right. Might try to get that band replaced with something that looks better.
So far I am loving the Misfit. Love hearing that customer support is helpful in case I have a problem, like many has, with the crystal shattering.
text_fidelity_b: Misfit Phase Hybrid Wearables Smartwatch - Rose Gold
